issue.title: [Bug]: Cover letter agent has no "don't invent candidate facts" rule, and the AI critic's fabrication check never sees the profile
issue.body:
## Summary

The generated cover letter states achievements the candidate never provided. In our run the profile said only "Built and maintained ETL pipelines using Python and Airflow; optimized Redshift queries", and the letter (Traditional Chinese) claimed:

- 每日處理數百萬筆資料 ("processing millions of records per day")
- 透過索引調整與查詢改寫，將關鍵報表產出時間縮短約 40% ("cut key report generation time by about 40% through index tuning and query rewrites")
- 協助建立資料驗證流程，減少人工檢查錯誤 ("helped build a data-validation process that reduced manual checking errors"), attached to the AnalyticsCo role, which only listed "Developed SQL scripts for reporting"

The full résumé text was in the prompt. Nothing was truncated, so the model invented these numbers rather than misreading the input.

This is not a one-off. We re-ran the same test case twice more on the same Jobsmith source (2026-10-20, DeepSeek via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Each letter invented different facts:

- Both letters gave the candidate a made-up Chinese name ("陳彥廷" in one run, "陳奕辰" in the other). The profile only says "Alex Chen".
- One letter says the candidate "在 104 與 CakeResume 上看到貴公司招募" ("saw your opening on 104 and CakeResume"). No job board was fetched; the phrase came from untrusted text quoted in the input.
- Both added operational details the profile doesn't contain, such as daily/hourly schedules, failure retries and data-quality checks.

A user who sends this letter is making false claims to an employer. Jobsmith already guards against this in other places: `resume.py` and `refine.py` forbid inventing experience, and the critic is meant to check for it. Neither guard covers the cover letter:

1. **The cover letter prompt has no grounding rule for candidate facts.** `app/agents/cover_letter.py:6-11` (`COVER_SYSTEM`) asks the model to "凸顯求職者的相關經歷" (highlight the candidate's relevant experience). The only anti-fabrication sentence covers company facts ("沒有公司情報就不要杜撰"). In contrast, `app/agents/resume.py:10` says "嚴禁捏造求職者沒有的經歷；只能重組與強調既有內容", and `app/agents/refine.py:15,22` say "不可捏造未提供的經歷".
2. **The AI critic can't detect fabrication.** `app/agents/critic.py:15` lists "是否有捏造未提供的經歷" (whether any unprovided experience was fabricated) as a criterion. However, `critique_package` (`critic.py:22-40`) only sends `【職缺】` plus the generated documents, never the candidate profile. The reviewer has nothing to compare the letter against, so it cannot tell a real "40%" from an invented one. This affects users who enable quality review, and the CLI, where `quality_review` is `True` by default (`app/cli.py:101`).

All references are to `main` @ f5427c156d4d0289463f048a2beedb87c80e802b (still the latest commit on `master` as of 2026-10-20).

## Steps to reproduce

**A. Prompt contents (deterministic, no model calls).** From the repository root:

```python
# repro_capture.py: stub the LLM and print what the cover-letter and critic calls send
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import app.agents.cover_letter as cl, app.agents.critic as cr
from app.models import ParsedJob, Profile, CoverLetter, CritiqueReport
captured = []
class Fake:
    def __init__(self, s): self.s = s
    def invoke(self, msgs):
        captured.append(msgs)
        return CoverLetter(body="...") if self.s is CoverLetter else CritiqueReport(
            resume_score=100, cover_letter_score=90, interview_score=100, overall_pass=True, feedback=[])
class LLM:
    def with_structured_output(self, s): return Fake(s)
cl.get_llm = cr.get_llm = lambda tier: LLM()
job = ParsedJob(title="Senior Data Engineer", company="Finlytics", required_skills=["Python", "SQL"])
profile = Profile(name="Alex Chen", skills=["Python", "SQL", "Airflow", "AWS"],
                  raw_text="Data Engineer at DataWorks (2020-present): Built ETL pipelines with Airflow; optimized Redshift queries.")
cl.write_cover_letter(job, profile, None)
cr.critique_package(job, cover_letter=CoverLetter(body="...cut report time by 40%, millions of rows/day..."))
print("cover prompt has candidate-fact rule:", any(k in captured[0][0][1] for k in ("捏造", "未提供的經歷")))
print("critic sees profile:", "Airflow" in captured[1][1][1] or "Alex Chen" in captured[1][1][1])
print("critic sections:", [l for l in captured[1][1][1].splitlines() if l.startswith("【")])
```

Output:

```
cover prompt has candidate-fact rule: False
critic sees profile: False
critic sections: ['【職缺】', '【求職信】']
```

**B. End-to-end.** Generate a cover letter (CLI or Web) for a profile whose experience lines contain no numbers, for example "Built and maintained ETL pipelines using Python and Airflow; optimized Redshift queries." The letter frequently adds concrete scale or percentage claims that are not in the profile.

## Expected behavior

The cover letter only restates and emphasizes facts in the candidate profile, as the résumé tailor already does. When quality review is on, the critic receives the profile and can flag claims that the profile doesn't support.

## Actual behavior

The letter contains invented metrics ("millions of records per day", "about 40% faster reports"). If the critic runs, it cannot flag them because it never sees the profile.

## Suggested fix

- Add the same constraint the résumé agent uses to `COVER_SYSTEM`, for example: "只能使用求職者背景中提供的事實；嚴禁捏造未提供的經歷、數字或成果。沒有量化數據就不要自行補數字。" Consider adding it to `INTERVIEW_SYSTEM` too, because its STAR answers are built from the same profile.
- Pass the profile into `critique_package` (for example, `profile_prompt_json(profile)` as a `【求職者背景】` section) so the "是否有捏造未提供的經歷" criterion can actually be checked. Update `critic_node` in `app/graph.py` to pass `state["profile"]`.

## Environment

- Jobsmith `main` @ f5427c1, run in a Linux container. Graph entry point `app/graph.py:build_graph`, with `artifact_targets=["cover_letter"]`, `batch=True`, and no company research or critic.
- AI backend: openai / BYOK (OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Our runs used DeepSeek (`deepseek-chat`, then `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) rather than the default Claude tier. How often a model invents facts varies by model, but the prompt and critic gaps above are model-independent.

steps: Generate a cover letter for a Senior Data Engineer job at Finlytics (required skills Python, SQL) for candidate Alex Chen whose profile says only 'Built and maintained ETL pipelines using Python and Airflow; optimized Redshift queries.'
expected: The cover letter only uses facts present in the candidate's profile and job input, without inventing metrics, names or achievements.
defect: The generated cover letter states achievements and details the candidate never provided, e.g. 每日處理數百萬筆資料 ("processing millions of records per day"), a ~40% report-time reduction, or an invented Chinese name such as "陳彥廷".

fault location.explanation: The cover-letter system prompt asks the model to highlight the candidate's experience but only forbids inventing company facts; unlike resume.py (L10) and refine.py it has no rule against fabricating candidate experience.
The critic's fabrication criterion (CRITIC_SYSTEM L15) cannot work because the request only contains the job and the generated documents, never the candidate profile to compare against.

Root cause: INFERRED FROM SOURCE (no upstream fix found). write_cover_letter sends the job, the full candidate profile and any company brief to the model with COVER_SYSTEM, which tells it to write a Taiwanese-style cover letter that 凸顯求職者的相關經歷 (highlights the candidate's relevant experience) and only says not to invent company facts when no company brief is given. There is no instruction to stay within the provided candidate facts, whereas the resume and refine agents explicitly forbid fabricating experience, so the model embellishes the sparse profile with invented volumes, percentages, names and sources. The secondary guard does not help: critique_package lists fabrication as a criterion but builds its request from the job and the generated documents only, so the critic has no profile to compare against (and the ABB binding disables quality review anyway). Minimal fix: add a grounding rule to COVER_SYSTEM equivalent to resume.py's (嚴禁捏造求職者沒有的經歷；只能重組與強調既有內容, including no invented numbers/names), and include the candidate profile in critique_package's sections. Caveat: the first location is a prompt-level fix and the resulting behaviour remains model-dependent.
